headline: AI researcher Nathan Lambert and Tom Zick launched a nonprofit lab, Trillium Labs, to publish in full how frontier AI models are trained after their first stage.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a plan with named backers but no published work yet.
importance_line: Academic and independent researchers could gain open recipes for the training step that shapes how chatbots behave, but the lab has released nothing yet and is still seeking funding and computing power.
summary: EdTech Innovation Hub reports that Trillium Labs, a nonprofit co-founded by AI researcher Nathan Lambert and Tom Zick, plans to publish complete “post-training” recipes, meaning the data, code, tests and checkpoints used to shape a model after its first training, which frontier companies rarely share. It has early backing from Halcyon Futures and Schmidt Sciences and is still looking for more funding and computing resources.
